newsitem.title: ANGOLA: Angola expected to produce 6,000 T coffee in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Angola expected to produce 6,000 T coffee in 1997.

text.p: Angola is expected to produce 6,000 tonnes of commercial coffee in 1997, the country's Secretary of State for Coffee, Gilberto Lutucuta, said on Tuesday.
He told Angola's news agency Angop that most of the coffee was being produced in the provinces of Uige, Kwanza Norte and Kwanza Sul.
Angola's coffee industry, like many of its other sectors, is struggling to recover from two decades of civil war between the government and former rebel UNITA movement.
A 1994 peace treaty has bolstered agricultural output, although a serious lack of funding and millions of landmines scattered throughout the countryside continues to hamper production.
Before Angola's independence from Portugal in 1975, the country was the fourth largest producer of coffee worldwide.
In 1973 it exported 218,000 tonnes of coffee, 112,000 tonnes of maize and 28.6 tonnes of beans.
Official coffee production was halted during the war with most of the coffee territory held by UNITA.

Lutucuta said the country's coffee production levels could reach 12,000 tonnes if the government was able to extend its administration into coffee areas in Uige province, currently still held by the former rebels.
"The search for Angolan coffee on the international market is huge but currently there is no capacity to satisfy the demand," he said.
He added that Angola needed hefty financial support to relaunch its coffee sector.
